eyebrow: docker run is really two steps
code:
$ docker create --name catalog northbridge/catalog:1.4
a3f8e9c1b2d4...
$ docker start catalog
catalog
caption: create configures the container; start launches its main process. docker run does both at once.

code:
$ docker stop catalog      # SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 10s
catalog
$ docker restart catalog   # stop, then start again
catalog
$ docker kill catalog      # SIGKILL immediately
catalog
caption: stop gives the process a chance to exit cleanly; kill is reserved for one that's genuinely stuck.

code:
$ docker pause catalog
catalog
$ docker inspect --format='{{.State.Status}}' catalog
paused
caption: pause freezes every process via the host's cgroup freezer -- nothing runs, nothing exits.
